glossary.definition: (A) "Eligible education institution" means an institution described in 20 U.S.C. 1088(a)(1) or 1141(a), as amended, or an area vocational education school as defined in 20 U.S.C. 2471(4), as amended.
glossary.scope: As used in sections 329.11 to 329.14 of the Revised Code:

glossary.definition: (B) "Federal poverty line" has the same meaning as in section 5104.01 of the Revised Code.
glossary.scope: As used in sections 329.11 to 329.14 of the Revised Code:

glossary.definition: (C) "Fiduciary organization" means a nonprofit fundraising organization exempt from federal income taxation pursuant to 26 U.S.C. 501 (a) and (c)(3).
glossary.scope: As used in sections 329.11 to 329.14 of the Revised Code:

glossary.definition: (D) "Financial institution" includes a bank, trust company, savings and loan association, savings bank, or credit union authorized to do business under federal law or the laws of this state.
glossary.scope: As used in sections 329.11 to 329.14 of the Revised Code:

glossary.definition: (E) "Funds available" means the amount available to a fiduciary organization for the purpose of matching funds deposited by program participants.
glossary.scope: As used in sections 329.11 to 329.14 of the Revised Code:

glossary.definition: (F) "Individual development account" means a trust created or organized in the United States pursuant to an individual development account program established under section 329.12 of the Revised Code to enable an individual eligible to participate in the program to accumulate funds for the purposes specified in section 329.14 of the Revised Code.
glossary.scope: As used in sections 329.11 to 329.14 of the Revised Code:

glossary.definition: (G) "Nonprofit microenterprise program" means a program under which loans and assistance are provided to low-income persons for the purpose of starting or operating a small business.
glossary.scope: As used in sections 329.11 to 329.14 of the Revised Code:
As used in sections 329.11 to 329.14 of the Revised Code:

glossary.definition: (I) "Qualified acquisition costs" means the costs associated with acquiring, constructing, or reconstructing a residence, including any ordinary or reasonable settlement, financing, or other closing costs.
glossary.scope: As used in sections 329.11 to 329.14 of the Revised Code:

glossary.definition: (J) "Qualified business" means any business formed for a purpose for which persons lawfully may associate themselves.
glossary.scope: As used in sections 329.11 to 329.14 of the Revised Code:

glossary.definition: (K) "Qualified business plan" means a plan that includes a description of services or goods to be sold, a marketing plan, and projected financial statements.
